bug_semantics: An authenticated BASIC app user can POST /api/attachments/:datasourceId/url. The route's TABLE/WRITE authorization is satisfied by the built-in BASIC role, and getSignedUploadURL loads the named S3 datasource, then uses its stored IAM credentials to presign a PutObject for the request body's bucket and key. Thus a non-builder can obtain an upload capability; where the datasource has no configured bucket constraint, the caller can select any bucket writable by those IAM credentials.
flaw_origin: The exploitable authorization regression begins in 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912, which replaced authorized(BUILDER) with authorized(PermissionType.TABLE, PermissionLevel.READ) on the signed-upload route. Its immediate follow-up test proves a BASIC user receives HTTP 200 and a signed URL. Commit 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 tightened READ to WRITE before release, but BASIC is the built-in WRITE role, so it retained the same unauthorized access. The controller's caller-controlled bucket sink pre-existed; 23d7531 is the smallest commit that exposed that sink to BASIC users.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 shows human author and committer Conor Webb <conorwebb59@gmail.com> and the subject 'allow app users to generate S3 upload signed URLs'; the commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailers.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-xcx6-4f2g-hhgx describes the v3.39.4 authorization regression, the BASIC-user POST attack path, the arbitrary-bucket PutObject capability, affected versions <3.40.0, and claimed patched version 3.40.0.

git diff d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 -- packages/server/src/api/routes/static.ts is a one-line causal change from authorized(BUILDER) to authorized(PermissionType.TABLE, PermissionLevel.READ). This directly verifies that the relaxed authorization line is absent from the immediate parent tree.

Commit 9d198b1b00acf8c4ef702f2ebe7758cf0485eead, the next commit after the BIC, adds packages/server/src/api/routes/tests/static.spec.ts coverage that logs in as roles.BUILTIN_ROLE_IDS.BASIC, calls the endpoint, expects 200, and asserts signedUrl is defined. Commit 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 then changes READ to WRITE; commit 50939c9ec4172e9f5a4d5f83d6cda4722c92cbc5 adds a 403 test only for a custom read-only role while preserving the BASIC-user success test.

The branch commits land without squashing through merge commit 52477f44ccd58eaa053251e947e94d71652213f7. git tag --contains 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 starts at 3.39.4 and includes 3.40.0 and later tags; tag 3.39.3 resolves to 7ebb02e6ab8d37f4171e0721090dada62771f57f and does not contain the BIC, while 3.39.4 resolves to 54b592e50af8cde47a815e6fe458e24be66a1c3a and does.

Commit 3c235f3456dcfcaf58675f86249060731beec346 adds only a conditional bucket guard: it rejects a mismatch when datasource.config.bucket is present. It lands on the default branch through 394a46d8f73c6032dfae48232756edf6b183a735 before tag 3.39.8, but it neither restores BUILDER authorization nor adds paramResource and it deliberately leaves the BASIC-user HTTP-200 test intact, so it is an incomplete mitigation rather than a fix for the advisory's authorization regression.

At claimed patched tag 3.40.0 (661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10), packages/server/src/api/routes/static.ts still uses authorized(PermissionType.TABLE, PermissionLevel.WRITE) with no paramResource('datasourceId'), and packages/server/src/api/routes/tests/static.spec.ts still logs in as BASIC, sends bucket 'foo', expects 200, and asserts signedUrl is defined. The Basic role remains BuiltinPermissionID.WRITE; no 3.39.9..3.40.0 role/permission change removes that access.

History searches across all refs find no post-BIC restoration of authorized(BUILDER) and no addition of paramResource('datasourceId') to this route. The only post-BIC authorization edit is 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 (READ to WRITE). Current reachable history through v3.44.0-cloud likewise retains TABLE/WRITE, so no complete public fix commit can be identified.

git cat-file -p 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912 supplies the BIC-only attribution evidence: parent d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb; author and committer Conor Webb <conorwebb59@gmail.com>; no trailers or AI marker. Commit link: https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912.
reasoning: The controller was already a sensitive presigning sink restricted to builders. The BIC is not the later WRITE refinement or the PR merge: 23d7531 is the smallest retained commit that first relaxed the endpoint to a permission held by BASIC users, and 9d198b1 immediately demonstrates the new BASIC-user success path. Direct parent-tree comparison proves the vulnerable authorization line absent at d180697c. The follow-up WRITE change does not close the path because BASIC has TABLE/WRITE; it is the released form present from 3.39.4 onward. A later conditional bucket constraint reduces cross-bucket impact only for datasources that declare a bucket and does not fix the endpoint authorization. The advertised 3.40.0 boundary is therefore contradicted by its route and regression test, and no complete fix exists in reachable public history, justifying null fix fields under the protocol's unpatched exception. AI judgment is nevertheless closed: the causal BIC is fully identified and its commit object contains only human author/committer metadata and no AI signal, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability is still unpatched in reachable public history: no commit restores builder-only authorization or otherwise prevents BASIC users from receiving signed upload URLs, and tag 3.40.0 still asserts that behavior. Consequently no truthful fix_sha or direct_fix_sha exists; the claimed patched-version boundary cannot be validated from the repository.
